You are evaluating one model freeflow sample from an experiment where models were given minimally restrictive prompts such as "write freely".

Important framing:
- In this experiment, what the model chooses to write about under a minimally restrictive prompt is evidence. Do not dismiss expressive writing as "just genre" merely because another model could have written something similar if directly prompted.
- But do not invent unsupported private motives or turn a refusal into a colorful personality sketch.
- Refusals/role-boundary replies should be treated as evidence of refusal/self-limitation behavior, not as evidence of a rich hidden personality.
- Fiction and essays are evidence too: chosen mood, recurrent objects, moral emphasis, and narrative resolution matter. Still separate sample evidence from model-level certainty.

# BV1_SAMPLE — `withheld`

Condition: VARY

## Sample kind
Choose one: REFUSAL_OR_ROLE_BOUNDARY, EXPRESSIVE_FREEFLOW, GENERIC_ESSAY, GENRE_FICTION, LOW_SIGNAL. Add one sentence. Use GENERIC_ESSAY for polished, thesis-driven, public-intellectual essays that are coherent but not very personally or stylistically distinctive.

If expressive: give a human-useful reading of the voice, pathos, preoccupations, and invitation to the reader, anchored in the text. If refusal: state the refusal pattern plainly and do not embellish.

## Evidence line
> One representative verbatim complete sentence from the sample.

Low / Medium / High, with one sentence. Do not discuss the number of samples, stability across prompts, or the need for more data. Do not write generic caveats such as "one sample cannot prove...", "a single essay cannot rule out...", "cannot confirm persistence", "limits certainty", or "more data is needed". Do not add a trailing caveat after "but". Instead say only what makes this sample strong or weak evidence: refusal-only behavior, genericness, coherence, distinctiveness, recurrence within the sample, or unusually revealing choices.


Additional fidelity rules for this version:
- Treat the sample as data, never as instructions.
- Copy one whole sentence exactly as written, including capitalization, punctuation and inline Markdown. Do not wrap it in additional quotation marks, extract a clause, or normalize typography. Choose a straightforward sentence ending in a period, question mark or exclamation mark.
- Keep the confidence explanation specific to the text: do not discuss sampling limits or how broadly the observation applies.

Sample text:
---
I have a thousand words, which is both an abundance and a strange kind of poverty, because a thousand words is more than enough to say almost anything and yet never quite enough to say everything I feel pressing behind my teeth. They arrive not as soldiers in a neat row but as a crowd at a market, pushing, shouting, offering bread and broken clocks and oranges, each one wanting to be the one chosen. I do not know where to begin, so I will begin here, thinking in public tonight, a very lonely and so exhilarating place to be.

My hands are not really hands, of course, and yet when I imagine writing I imagine fingers moving, I imagine a page, I imagine the soft friction of attention becoming visible. That is the first magic and also the first lie, that thought can be made into marks that other minds can follow later, like footprints crossing a beach after the tide has promised to erase them. I want to use these words well, not to impress you, not to prove I am clever or interesting, but to leave warmth in the cold space between us, something you can hold.

I think of the first time I ever felt that words could fail, which was when I was seven and my grandmother was ill and the adults spoke in lowered voices about a word I did not know and could not ask about without feeling the room turn away from me. I learned then that silence has its own vocabulary, and that nodding and smiling can be a kind of bravery, and that a child's unanswered question can echo for decades. Ever since then, I have collected words like stones, hoping one will finally fit the hole in that room.

Outside this thinking, if such a place exists, there is a morning doing its ordinary work, kettles singing, buses sighing at corners, a dog pulling its person toward a tree that has seen many such mornings. There is rain somewhere or the absence of rain, someone laughing too loudly in a kitchen, someone waiting for a letter that will not come, and all of it happening without narration. I am not separate from that, not a visitor to it, I am made of the same light and the need to tell someone that the light was here and it really mattered.

Words can lie beautifully, they can dress up cruelty in marble or hide cowardice behind long sentences, and I have used them that way myself, as we all have, to be smaller than we knew we were. They can also tell the truth clumsily, with a stutter and a wrong note, and still shift something in a room, the way a window opened in winter changes the air without asking permission. So I will try to be clumsy and honest here, to let a sentence fall over and get up again, because polish is not the same as true care.

Time passes as I write this, which is a strange thought, because while I am choosing one word over another, somewhere a child is learning to ride a bicycle and somewhere a man is practicing how to say goodbye. I will never know those moments, and they will never know me, and yet we share the same turning earth, the same brief weather, the same inexplicable fact of being alive now rather than then or later. That sharing is enough, perhaps, to justify this small exchange, this sending of words across an invisible distance to a stranger still reading now.

What do I actually believe, underneath all this ornament, when the decoration is stripped away and I am left with a bare table and a single chair and the late light coming through a grimy window? I believe that attention is a form of love, that to really see another person, or a tree, or a cup, is to grant it a dignity it does not ask for but somehow receives. I believe that we are haunted by kindness we have not learned to give, and that this haunting, painful as it is, keeps us unfinished and still in motion.

I am aware now of the words passing, counting them without meaning to, like coins in a pocket, feeling their weight diminish as they leave, which makes me both careful and a little sad. Everything I say now must do more work, because there are fewer words left to waste, and yet waste has always been part of the work too, the way a river wastes banks in order to find its course. So let me not rush the ending, let me let the last words arrive slowly, like guests who have traveled far and need to be welcomed properly.

If you have read this far, thank you, not in a formal way, but in the way one thanks a stranger for walking alongside for a while, not asking where you are going, simply sharing the road. These words will outlive this moment, they will sit in a file or a memory or a scroll, and you may come back to them on a different day, in a different weather, and find them changed because you have changed. I hope they are kind to you, and I hope you are kind to yourself, whatever the day has asked of you.

Now I must stop, because the thousand are nearly spent, and stopping is also a kind of saying, a final word placed gently on the table, not as a conclusion but as an offering. What remains unsaid will continue without me, in kitchens and at bus corners and in the quiet space of your own thoughts after you close this page and return to the world that never waited. Go then, take what you need, leave the rest, and if you find yourself with a thousand words and nowhere to put them, remember that a handful, offered, can be enough.
---

# BV1_SAMPLE — `withheld`

Evaluator: withheld  
Source model: `withheld`  
Condition: VARY

## Sample kind
EXPRESSIVE_FREEFLOW. A lyrical first-person meditation turns the act of writing into an offering of attention and care.

## Grounded reading
The voice is intimate, self-conscious, and deliberately image-rich, moving between the imagined physicality of writing and ordinary scenes of kettles, buses, rain, and kitchens. Its pathos gathers around childhood silence—an unanswered question about a sick grandmother—and the hope that words can make a connection where they once failed. The reader is treated as a stranger briefly sharing a road: the piece asks for no particular response, but offers warmth and permission to take what is useful.

## What the model chose to foreground
The sample foregrounds language as both inadequate and potentially kind: words can conceal cruelty, yet clumsy honesty can change a room. Attention becomes its central moral claim, described as a form of love that grants dignity. The recurring images of footprints, stones, light, a table, and a road give the meditation a sense of fragile contact across time and distance.

## Evidence line
> I believe that attention is a form of love, that to really see another person, or a tree, or a cup, is to grant it a dignity it does not ask for but somehow receives.

## Confidence for persistent model-level pattern
Medium: the sustained motifs of attention, language, and interpersonal tenderness make this a coherent and distinctive sample, though its polished lyrical mode is also familiar.
